summary: The candidate is a substantial partial fix: it passes the exact issue fixture, all reviewed GLM literal counterexamples, its focused regression, and the full function-call suite. It does not fully implement one-shot/streaming parity because Mistral loses later calls in a valid JSON array when commas are not followed by spaces.

tests.what_was_measured: Original issue reproduction on the recorded prepared base; GLM-family type corruption, missing MiniMax call, and Step3 extra-call mismatch reproduced. The script's aggregation masks two other reported classes.
All eight exact supplied fixtures reported parity at the candidate commit.
Full function-call suite: 550 passed, 1,596 subtests passed.
Independent literal and chunk-boundary parity checks. GLM-family cases passed; all 181 Mistral compact-JSON chunkings failed because later calls became normal text.

gpu_execution.evidence: No GPU was used because all changed and reviewed behavior is deterministic Python parser logic.

remaining_counterexamples: Mistral detect_and_parse accepts valid JSON arrays whose object separators are ',' with no following space, but parse_streaming_increment recognizes only the literal ', ' separator. Whole-increment, character-at-a-time, and every two-way split delivery return only the first call and leak later calls into normal_text.
remaining_limitations: No tokenizer/model or HTTP serving path was exercised; deterministic parser text was supplied directly.
No semantic accuracy, full-model, multi-GPU, or distributed behavior was tested.
The prepared host is ROCm 7.2/gfx950 rather than CUDA/RTX 4090; the reviewed code path is architecture-independent, but no cross-architecture serving claim is made.
No native rebuild was performed because the candidate changes only Python and report/test files.
